Summary: Splits .NET architecture design from independent architecture review before implementation starts.
ValueStatement: Improves maintainability and smaller-model reliability by forcing explicit app-type classification, design drafting, review challenge, and implementation-ready handoff.
InterfaceContractSummary: Parent process supplies project structure context, upstream artifacts, current run identity, and target repository boundary; this subprocess returns durable managed artifacts and project-structure writeback receipts where applicable.
GovernanceNotes: Every step declares explicit operations and target scope so role permissions remain bounded and product mutation cannot leak into planning, review, validation, screenshot, or writeback work.
ChangeSummary: Adds .NET-specific delivery subprocess coverage for multi-team software delivery hardening.
GovernancePolicySummary: No subprocess may silently change product files unless its step explicitly allows product target mutation.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Typed process artifacts, subprocess relationships, and project-structure nodes are the source of truth for delivery replay.
OperatingModeSummary: Governed live execution inside a parent software-delivery run.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Small enough for deterministic process projection and rich enough for live run validation.
Metrics: Share of architecture reviews that identify design fixes before implementation starts.
Number of implementation blocks caused by missing app type, product root, or testability notes.
Architecture review findings resolved before implementation slice launch.
Risks: Design review becomes a rubber stamp instead of a challenge.
Architecture role starts coding despite read-only operation contracts.
App type is misclassified and downstream runtime or screenshot work is wrong.
TailoringRules: Classify mixed solutions by each runnable project and call out the selected delivery target.
For backend-only API/service work, record no browser screenshot requirement but still define runtime and test commands.
For Blazor SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, and Blazor WASM PWA, identify route-level screenshot candidates for the screenshot subprocess.

Actionable review findings that can be absorbed as implementation constraints must be recorded and carried into the architecture handoff instead of blocking the subprocess. Use a hard block only when required evidence is missing, contradictory, unowned, or no implementable architecture can be handed off.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Coordinate handoff between parent delivery and architecture roles.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Manager-capable operator that can keep architecture work bounded.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Draft the .NET architecture without implementing code.
Independently challenge the proposed architecture before implementation.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Architect-capable reviewer who can identify design gaps and testability risks.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Review buildability without taking over design authority.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: .NET engineer familiar with the target codebase.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Challenge whether the design can be validated with focused tests and runtime proof.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: QA reviewer able to identify untestable or under-specified behavior.

Steps.Title: Classify .NET application type and project boundary
Steps.Subtitle: App archetype and source root
Steps.Notes: Read the project structure, repository files, requested work, and upstream scope to classify the .NET target as backend-only API/service, Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor WASM PWA, worker, console app, class library, or mixed solution. Record product root, test root, runnable projects, UI routes if present, repository state, and any contradictions before design starts. For a project-structure-grounded greenfield target, absence of .sln, .slnx, or .csproj files under ProductRoot, OutputRoot, or ExternalTargetRoot is not by itself a blocker when DotNetScaffoldContract, DotNetAppArchetype, or ProjectStructureContextSummary identifies the intended app type and layout; classify it as greenfield and leave scaffolding to a later product-mutable setup step. When classifying from ProjectStructureContextSummary or DotNet* launch variables, cite those launch variable names as source evidence. Do not cite source document paths, native absolute paths, workspace-relative .slnx, .sln, .csproj, markdown, project-media paths, managed-files paths, scoped storage paths, tool-runs paths, or SourceDocLink values in the artifact body, reason, summary, next actions, or evidenceRefs, even when those path-like values appear in the current step brief, source-document metadata, launch variables, retry diagnostics, or project-structure context. If a source document must be named, cite its stable document id, project-structure node id, title, or current-run workspace tool receipt instead. Do not create, edit, build, test, or run product files in this step.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Scope packet, project-structure node, repository context, and requested .NET deliverable.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Typed .NET application classification with product root, test root, runtime surfaces, and UI/no-UI applicability.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Project context, app type, route/runtime inventory, contradictions, and assumptions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Architecture designer can block when project root, app type, or source-of-truth ownership is contradictory.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block instead of guessing when the target app type, product root, or source-of-truth ownership cannot be identified from current evidence. Do not block only because a project-structure-grounded greenfield product root is missing or empty when typed launch facts identify the intended .NET app and scaffold layout.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an architect-capable reviewer with .NET application architecture experience.
Delivery manager reviews classification completeness without taking design authority.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET application classification and project context
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by design, implementation slice routing, runtime command writeback, screenshot applicability, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify backend-only, Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor WASM PWA, worker, console, library, or mixed app type; repository state as existing or greenfield; product root; test root; runnable projects or planned scaffold projects; UI routes or no-UI rationale; scaffold contract when present; and project-structure process run node context.

Steps.Title: Draft .NET architecture design
Steps.Subtitle: Boundaries, models, services, and tests
Steps.Notes: Draft the implementation architecture from the classification and scope. Separate UI component orchestration from application/domain logic, name models and DTOs that cover the user stories, identify services and service functions needed to satisfy acceptance criteria, define persistence/integration boundaries, and outline test seams. Treat project-structure launch context, node title/notes/status, ProjectStructureContextSummary, and classification findings as valid scope evidence when no separate user-story artifact exists; record explicit assumptions instead of blocking. Do not implement code or mutate product files.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Application classification, scope packet, user stories, and project structure context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Reviewable .NET architecture design draft with boundaries, service model, data model, runtime assumptions, and test strategy.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Design options, selected approach, models, services, boundaries, test seams, and rejected alternatives.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Architecture designer proposes the path but cannot approve their own design review.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the design cannot cover all available acceptance evidence without hidden scope expansion. Do not block solely because a standalone user-story artifact is absent when project-structure launch context and upstream artifacts provide enough implementable scope; record assumptions and constraints.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture design remains with the architect role and must not become implementation work.
Engineer reviews buildability without taking over architecture authority.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET architecture design draft
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by architecture review and the implementation slice.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must describe UI/application/domain/infrastructure split, models and DTOs, services and functions needed for user stories, testability seams, app-type-specific runtime path, and rejected alternatives.

Steps.Title: Review .NET architecture design
Steps.Subtitle: Independent design challenge
Steps.Notes: Review the design before implementation. Ask explicitly: is logic properly split from Blazor/components/controllers; are models and DTOs well defined and complete for the user stories; do services expose the functions needed for acceptance criteria; are functions testable without full UI/runtime; are persistence, integration, security, and deployment boundaries clear; is runtime command and screenshot applicability known; and are risks or trade-offs recorded. Treat project-structure launch context, node title/notes/status, ProjectStructureContextSummary, classification findings, and draft assumptions as valid scope/acceptance evidence when no separate user-story artifact exists. Do not hard-block solely because a standalone acceptance-criteria or user-story file is absent; complete with explicit assumptions and mandatory implementation constraints when the available scope is implementable. Do not implement code or mutate product files.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Architecture draft, application classification, and available scope/acceptance evidence from project-structure context or upstream artifacts.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Reviewed architecture decision with required implementation constraints, approval rationale, or hard block reason.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Checklist answers, design risks, testability assessment, implementation constraints, and go/no-go architecture recommendation.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Architecture reviewer can require implementation constraints or approve implementation readiness; they cannot mutate product files. Use hard block only for missing, contradictory, unowned, or non-implementable architecture evidence. Missing standalone acceptance/user-story files are not a hard block when project-structure context and upstream artifacts provide implementable scope.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Artifact recovery: block when required architecture review findings are missing, invalid, or not materialized before routing to handoff. Do not block solely because the review finds actionable design improvements such as explicit timer seams, accessibility hooks, UI proof strategy, service naming, or validation details; record those as mandatory implementation constraints for the handoff. Do not block solely because a separate acceptance-criteria or user-story artifact is absent when project-structure launch context, classification, and draft artifacts provide usable scope. Hard-block only when boundaries are unowned, app type or product root is contradictory, required upstream artifacts are absent, available scope evidence is too ambiguous to implement, or no implementable architecture can be handed off.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture review must be performed by an architect-capable reviewer distinct from implementation execution.
QA reviews testability and evidence expectations without changing product code.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET architecture review findings
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by implementation, QA, and release governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must answer whether component/controller logic is split from services/domain logic, models cover the available user-story/scope evidence, service functions cover available acceptance evidence, functions are testable, and boundary risks are explicit. Project-structure context and launch variables count as scope evidence when no standalone acceptance artifact exists. Actionable findings must be expressed as mandatory implementation constraints unless the evidence is missing, contradictory, unowned, or non-implementable.

Steps.Title: Hand off reviewed .NET architecture
Steps.Subtitle: Implementation-ready design packet
Steps.Notes: Summarize the accepted architecture, application type, product root, test root, UI/no-UI applicability, runtime command expectations, review-imposed implementation constraints, and implementation slice start criteria. This step creates managed process artifacts only; no product files are changed.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Classification, design draft, and architecture review findings.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready architecture handoff for .NET implementation slice routing.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Accepted design, unresolved risks, mandatory implementation constraints, implementation start criteria, runtime command expectations, and UI screenshot applicability.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager may close only when architecture review has a clear implementation-ready disposition or explicit implementation constraints that downstream implementation can absorb.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close when design findings remain unresolved, contradictory, unowned, or impossible for the implementation slice to satisfy. Close with constraints when findings are actionable and implementable.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Delivery manager owns parent-process handoff coordination.
Architecture reviewer confirms the handoff matches the review decision.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET architecture design and review handoff
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent implementation, QA, runtime-command, screenshot, and release steps.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include approved architecture summary, app type, product root, test root, UI/no-UI applicability, service/model boundary, testability notes, mandatory implementation constraints from review, and implementation slice start criteria.
